stem: Which of the following best describes the welfare reform law President Clinton signed in 1996?

options.text: It created a new federal jobs guarantee for every unemployed American
options.misconception: The law ended the federal welfare guarantee; it created no jobs guarantee.

options.text: It doubled federal welfare payments and removed all time limits
options.misconception: The law did the opposite — it ended open-ended aid and imposed time limits.

options.text: It transferred welfare entirely to private charities
options.misconception: Welfare stayed a government program; the law shifted its administration to the states.

options.text: It ended the federal guarantee of welfare aid and added work requirements

rationales.A: Background: the law ended the federal welfare guarantee; it created no jobs guarantee.
rationales.B: Background: the law did the opposite — it ended open-ended aid and imposed time limits.
rationales.C: Background: welfare stayed a government program; the law shifted its administration to the states.
rationales.D: Background: the 1996 reform ended welfare as a federal entitlement, let states set their own rules, and required recipients to begin work after two years.
rationales.general:
1. Start with what 'welfare reform' meant in 1996: an end, not an expansion.
2. Background: the law ended the federal welfare guarantee and shifted administration to the states.
3. Background: it required recipients to begin work after two years — the 'workfare' rule.
4. Nothing was doubled, privatized, or guaranteed; the guarantee itself was what ended.
Remember: 1996 ended welfare as an entitlement and added work rules.
